_note: Snapshot of jfall.nl/timetable-2026 (Sessionize) for J-Fall 2026 (12 November 2026, Pathé Ede). Opening, breaks and other service blocks are excluded. Co-speakers reduced to primary speaker to fit the one-speaker-per-session model. Abstracts shortened to their first sentences.

speakers.name: Willem Jan Glerum
speakers.bio: Principal Software Engineer at Lunatech. Focused on Quarkus, cloud, and security.

sessions.title: The Spring Test Profiler: Cut Down Your Test Execution Time by 70%
sessions.speaker: Philip Riecks
sessions.abstract: AI writes your code in seconds. Then you wait twenty minutes for CI to tell you whether it works. The bottleneck has moved: writing code is cheap, but verifying it against a slow build is now what stands between you and fast feedback.

sessions.title: On-premises AI: Frontier-level agentic engineering at the Dutch National Police
sessions.speaker: Miel van Welzen
sessions.abstract: Being a software engineer at a highly regulated organization can be frustrating. Especially last year, when new frontier models arrived almost weekly, while many of us were not allowed to use them at work (for good reasons).

sessions.title: How AI Lost the Thread: The Strange Path from Neurons to LLMs
sessions.speaker: Tineke Slotegraaf
sessions.abstract: In 1943 a neurophysiologist and a logician sketched the “artificial neuron”, AI’s founding myth. Ever since we use the brain and our intelligence as a metaphor for machine learning. But real neurons are noisy and chemical. There is no biological mechanism for backpropagation or transformers.

sessions.title: Don't fall in the metrics trap
sessions.speaker: Maarten Mulders
sessions.abstract: Many of us have experience with organisations where teams are assessed based on the number of story points or stories they complete. We also know what usually happens next: teams focus on delivering the "right" number of points to avoid scrutiny from management.

sessions.title: Modernizing a 2M+ LOC Java Monolith with Agentic AI: What Worked, What Failed, and How We Recovered
sessions.speaker: Marek Dominiak
sessions.abstract: Modernizing a 2M+ line Java monolith meant much more than upgrading Java, Spring, Hibernate, and Elasticsearch. We also had to deal with tightly coupled dependencies, abandoned libraries, outdated patterns, and features that had been too risky to change for years.

sessions.title: Level Up Your Java Streams with Gatherers
sessions.speaker: Hinse ter Schuur
sessions.abstract: Since Java 8, the Stream API has been a valuable tool for Java developers. However, our hunt for better solutions has often left us wanting more. Until now, we could only use the standard provided intermediate operations on streams, like map, filter, and flatMap.

sessions.title: Practical MCP Security in Action
sessions.speaker: Willem Jan Glerum
sessions.abstract: MCP authorization is OAuth 2.1 done right. Quarkus makes it tractable. Governance matters more than the token format.

sessions.title: Why am I here?
sessions.speaker: Jeroen van der Wal
sessions.abstract: You've felt it too, right? You describe what you want, answer some questions and AI writes it, and it does a pretty good job! Sometimes better than I would do and at least a lot quicker. But then the question comes up; if this can be done just by describing what you want, then, why am I here...?

sessions.title: From Specification to Production: Engineering in the Age of AI
sessions.speaker: Venkat Subramaniam
sessions.abstract: Now that AI can generate a lot of code, what does software engineering look like? What are the benefits of using AI and, more important, what are the risks and how to mitigate those?

sessions.title: Developing with AI: What if it were as simple as adding a library?
sessions.speaker: Stéphane Philippart
sessions.abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into our applications can seem much more complex than simply using AI tools in our daily lives. Do I need to learn a new language or adopt an entirely new technology stack?

sessions.title: Hack Your Brain: Smarter Learning for Devs
sessions.speaker: Simone de Gijt
sessions.abstract: This talk explores how developers can learn smarter, not harder, by applying insights from neuroscience to coding practice. You’ll discover why learning is more than storing information.

sessions.title: Your coding agent is a while loop!
sessions.speaker: Bruno Bossola
sessions.abstract: Most of us let an agent write our code every day, but almost none of us have ever opened one. So we guess what is inside: a planner, an orchestrator, a state machine, something very clever... There is nothing clever in there. There is a loop. A very simple one, also.

sessions.title: Evolving Language Defaults in Kotlin and Other Languages
sessions.speaker: Michail Zarečenskij
sessions.abstract: When designing a programming language, we decide what’s safe, what’s convenient, and what’s practical. These choices become our defaults, the way we believe most programs should be written in that language. However, defaults evolve over time.

sessions.title: Back to the Future: Building a RAG-Powered VR Time Machine
sessions.speaker: Susanne Pieterse
sessions.abstract: Step through a portal into Utrecht, 1528. Put on a VR headset and suddenly you're standing among monuments that no longer exist, with an all-knowing guide ready to answer any question you ask.

sessions.title: Scotty I need Warp Speed - Ways to improve JVM startup
sessions.speaker: Gerrit Grunwald
sessions.abstract: When running Java in the cloud, the JVM startup time can become a limitation. Especially when you look at spinning up new instances of an app as response to changes in load, the warmup time can be a problem.

sessions.title: Four ways to serve a drink: Plain calls, RAG, agents and MCP in Quarkus
sessions.speaker: Maarten Vandeperre
sessions.abstract: At some point someone asks you to "add a bit of AI" to your application. It sounds easy. Then the buzzwords arrive: RAG, agents, tool calling, MCP. Every vendor tells you that you need all of them. You don't. In this session we want to show you why, with running code instead of slides.

sessions.title: 6000 tests, 25 times a day, 365 days a year - All for quality
sessions.speaker: Sven Haster
sessions.abstract: Topicus KeyHub is an on-premise Jakarta EE11 serverside web IAM-application that is used by (among others) Logius, several municipalities, and Voys. KeyHub has high standards for quality and aims to achieve these with, among other things, a large battery of automated tests.

sessions.title: State of Confusion: Data Ownership in Event-Driven Systems
sessions.speaker: Jeroen Rosenberg
sessions.abstract: In event-driven systems you should not call another service's API but instead consume its events and maintain local state. However, how much state should you store?

sessions.title: Spring Cleaning: What Boot 4 Lets You Delete
sessions.speaker: Dan Vega
sessions.abstract: It is now more important than ever to stay up to date and patched on open source software. If you are upgrading to Spring Boot 4 there's a decent chance you're maintaining three or four things that are now unnecessary, and nobody on your team told you.

sessions.title: Getting more out of Maven
sessions.speaker: Marit van Dijk
sessions.abstract: Maven is an ubiquitous build tool in the Java ecosystem, some even claim it’s the de facto standard build tool. Configuring Maven is deceptively simple, after all it’s just a matter of writing XML, isn’t it? Things look differently when the rubber meets the road.

sessions.title: Senior Engineer, Still Failing
sessions.speaker: Sanne Noordzij
sessions.abstract: Not every problem can or should be fixed by writing perfect code. I spent years believing it could and should. I had the title, the experience, and the track record to prove it. By every visible measure, I was a senior software engineer.

sessions.title: Context Is a Budget - Spend It Wisely
sessions.speaker: Soham Dasgupta
sessions.abstract: AI coding assistants are now a daily tool, but most teams use them unstructured, i.e., pasting whole repos, leaving giant chats running for days, and reflexively reaching for the most expensive model.

sessions.title: Continuous Delivery: From fragmented pipelines to zero touch delivery
sessions.speaker: Anand Shukla
sessions.abstract: This session outlines a strategic shift from fragmented, team-owned deployment scripts to standardized, platform-driven Continuous Delivery (CD).

sessions.title: Teaching a New Dog Old Tricks: Give the Agent a Debugger
sessions.speaker: Anton Arhipov
sessions.abstract: When code misbehaves, coding agents often fall back on an old habit. They add print statements. The method works. It also changes the program before the agent understands the problem. The debugger provides a cleaner way to find the evidence.

sessions.title: How Can Java Applications Leverage Ahead-of-Time Caching
sessions.speaker: Ana Maria Mihalceanu
sessions.abstract: Starting with JDK 24, Project Leyden features moved from OpenJDK innovations into mainstream Java frameworks. Spring Boot, Quarkus, Helidon, and others adopted ahead-of-time caching, integrated it into their lifecycle, and published benchmarks that demonstrate substantial improvements.

sessions.title: Don't drown in your connection pool
sessions.speaker: Jos Roseboom
sessions.abstract: In this ByteSize talk, we'll start a Spring Boot application and use its connection pool log lines as our agenda. Instead of going through every setting, we'll pick the ones that are easy to misunderstand and the ones that can get you into serious trouble. No exhaustive configuration reference.

sessions.title: Java Citizens in the World of Mainframe
sessions.speaker: Valeriya Komarnitskaya
sessions.abstract: Every few years someone declares mainframe dead. And every few years, it's still running millions of transactions at heart of global banking, insurance and payments. This talk makes the case that the mainframe isn't the obstacle to modernisation: it can be used to approach transformation.

sessions.title: Java over Markdown: Specs That Compile
sessions.speaker: Adam Bien
sessions.abstract: The weights of every major LLM already incorporate Java conventions and best practices. A convention-over-configuration codebase requires no explanation because the structure itself serves as the prompt.

sessions.title: Don't Let Your Architecture Drift
sessions.speaker: Gunter Rotsaert
sessions.abstract: As codebases grow, how do you ensure that architectural decisions remain intact? That’s where ArchUnit comes in. By expressing architectural rules as tests, ArchUnit lets you verify your architecture automatically with every build. Taikai takes this concept further.

sessions.title: From Specs to Decks: A Tale of Bugs, DJs & the Importance of Hobbies
sessions.speaker: Lucía Conde-Moreno
sessions.abstract: Are you already feeling the conference information overload, but you feel guilty about taking a break? You definitely should join me for a few minutes of replacing SQL drops with EDM drops!

sessions.title: Voice UI's, AI, and the future of usability
sessions.speaker: Ramona Domen
sessions.abstract: When interacting with technology, most of it is done via a visual medium, yet for us humans, speech is the more native form of communication.

sessions.title: 5 vibe-coded games in 5 minutes
sessions.speaker: Pim Tegelaar
sessions.abstract: In this ignite session, I will showcase 5 vibe-coded games in 5 minutes. For each game I will show what I did wrong and how I solved it with the right prompts and the right models.

sessions.title: JVM startup in the age of disposable infra
sessions.speaker: Erik Steenman
sessions.abstract: We used to name our servers and nurse them like pets for years. Now our apps may run on infra that's gone after a few minutes. In this environment, we can no longer rely on the JVM to optimize our app's performance over time, and how fast we can start new instances matters more than ever.

sessions.title: Why I
sessions.speaker: Maarten Mulders
sessions.abstract: Of course, we are at this conference because we love the Java programming language and the Java ecosystem. But there are other worlds out there, ready for us to explore. Join me on this fast-paced exploration of one of them and see why I fell in love...

sessions.title: AI-architecture speedrun: from Woolly Wonka to Spaghetti Mario
sessions.speaker: Frederieke Scheper
sessions.abstract: Imagine a Scrum team with an overdue integration: combine external data with their own and get it into production next sprint. The pressure is real. Of course they reach for AI to move faster. Twenty slides. Fifteen seconds each. No pausing, no going back.

sessions.title: How A Friend Convinced Me To Buy My Own Domain
sessions.speaker: Rico Apon
sessions.abstract: For years I published my side projects on free hosting and just lived with the clunky greent13.github.io/elitefour links it generated for me. Buying a domain felt like a waste of money for what were, after all, just unfinished hobby projects that never felt professional enough to deserve one.

sessions.title: Designing a Lego model, or how my relaxing hobby turned out to be a software project in disguise
sessions.speaker: Jan Ouwens
sessions.abstract: Last year I was featured in the local newspaper with my hobby project: a Lego skyline model I designed for my home town. In this session I will show you how I kept cost down while designing, prototyping and optimis,oh no, it's a software project now.

sessions.title: Let's get Physical
sessions.speaker: Iulia Feroli
sessions.abstract: Surely LLMs didn’t peak at generating our emails and planning a trip itinerary. For those who want to see AI do something more meaningful, and let’s face it - way cooler, Physical AI is what you’ve secretly been needing.

sessions.title: Workshop: Designing Production-Ready Multi-Agent Systems with Spring AI
sessions.speaker: Raphael De Lio
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, we’re going to explore how to build a multi-agent system from the ground up using Spring AI. You’ll learn how to get multiple agents working together , each with its own role, memory, and context , all inside a clean, production-ready architecture.

sessions.title: 7 Ways You Can Build an Amazing Dev Career in the AI Era
sessions.speaker: Bruno Souza
sessions.abstract: Are you also wondering where you fit in all of this? Every day, you are bombarded with claims that AI will transform software development. Is this an unprecedented opportunity or an existential threat?

sessions.title: Java 26 and 27 are boring, and that's a good thing
sessions.speaker: Johannes Bechberger
sessions.abstract: Java’s predictable release cycle avoids big surprises. This predictability is one of Java’s strengths. While some other platforms introduce dramatic changes or even break existing code, JDK 26 and 27 deliver a set of small, practical improvements.

sessions.title: Emergent DevEx: The Good, the Bad, and the Legacy
sessions.speaker: Makan Sepehrifar
sessions.abstract: What happens when an organization grows from a few co-founders into 10,000 people? In a big organization, the developer experience isn't something you sit down and design. It's the sum of countless small changes, layered year after year.

sessions.title: Powering Personalization: How we built our Generic Decision Engine
sessions.speaker: Rick Ossendrijver
sessions.abstract: Generalization and personalization are at the core of how we build software at Picnic.

sessions.title: Java is Coming for Python’s Lunch: The Rise of JVM AI Agents
sessions.speaker: Frederik Pietzko
sessions.abstract: Unfortunately, for the past couple of years, Java developers have felt like second-class citizens in the AI space. While Python has dominated the headlines, we’ve been left wondering if we’ll need to rewrite our entire stack to create even a mediocre autonomous agent.

sessions.title: Keeping data private in real-time pipelines
sessions.speaker: Olena Kutsenko
sessions.abstract: We all love real-time data , clicks, payments, rides, messages , but most of it comes with a catch: it contains personal information we’re not supposed to leak, such as names, emails, locations, or even small clues that can identify someone.

sessions.title: Apache Camel as integration framework
sessions.speaker: Ferrie Bank
sessions.abstract: For years Apache Camel has been popular with integration specialists. Camel offers practical solutions for connecting Java clients to endpoints, for setting up rule-based routing of data, and for implementing enterprise integration patterns.

sessions.title: Finding and Fixing Issues with Legacy Code using AI
sessions.speaker: Venkat Subramaniam
sessions.abstract: AI is a great tool to generate ideas more and one area where we need a broad range of ideas is in identifying and fixing issues with code. The reality is that we all have to deal with legacy code, stuff written by someone who has left the company or those written in a hurry before that vacation.

sessions.title: Eval Driven Development: Why you need it to make your Agentic Application survive Production
sessions.speaker: Urs Peter
sessions.abstract: Agentic systems unlock capabilities that traditional “deterministic” applications simply can’t deliver.

sessions.title: Exploring Value Objects from Project Valhalla
sessions.speaker: Balkrishna Rawool
sessions.abstract: Project Valhalla is an important project at OpenJDK. The main features of the project are value objects, null-restricted types, parametric JVM and unification of primitives and classes. Together, they represent a fundamental shift in how the JVM manages memory and data.

sessions.title: Engineering the Harness: From Vibe Coding to Verified Code Generation
sessions.speaker: Ario Afrashteh
sessions.abstract: An AI agent writes good code when it knows what good means in your codebase. Usually it does not.

sessions.title: We Put Minecraft in a Browser Tab, Here's How the JVM Got There
sessions.speaker: Elisabeth Panholzer
sessions.abstract: Java was never meant to run inside a modern browser tab. In this session, we’ll show you how it does anyway, and just how far that idea can be pushed.

sessions.title: How to guard your AI agent without babysitting it?
sessions.speaker: Jos Roseboom
sessions.abstract: Your AI coding agent is impressive, but checking every permission request and hitting ‘Yes’ is annoying. Dangerously skip permissions solves that right away, but something like ‘rm -rf’ might give you other headaches… Will instructions to the agent prevent that? Is a local sandbox enough?

sessions.title: 4 years of Quarkus in production, what have we learned?
sessions.speaker: Jago de Vreede
sessions.abstract: Quarkus has rapidly gained popularity, but what's it really like to use it in an enterprise environment? This talk moves past the "Hello World" demos to share hard-earned lessons from over three years of building and maintaining enterprise-level applications with Quarkus.

sessions.title: Java, scripted?
sessions.speaker: Johan Hutting
sessions.abstract: Java 25 delivered a simplified approach to building software with JEP-512, primarily aimed at making the language more accessible. Yet this also offers experienced engineers the opportunity for simplified scripting using the power of the JVM along with their knowledge and skills in the language.

sessions.title: Java in 5 Microseconds: Inside a Crypto Trading Engine
sessions.speaker: Oleg Lobanov
sessions.abstract: What does it take to rebuild the core of a crypto exchange while it is already operating 24/7? In 2018, Bitvavo’s exchange ran on a familiar startup stack: Node.js, Go, Redis, MySQL, and Kafka.

sessions.title: Cracking the Code Review
sessions.speaker: Paco van Beckhoven
sessions.abstract: Code reviews are vital for ensuring good code quality and fostering teamwork. They serve as one of our last lines of defense against bugs and subpar code reaching production.

sessions.title: Generics - You Never Know What You’re Gonna Get
sessions.speaker: Bram Janssens
sessions.abstract: Many Java developers,even seasoned ones,struggle with generics and variance, often relying on guesswork when facing wildcards like ? extends or ? super. I know the feeling: I’ve been there myself, and now, as a teacher, I’ve seen how common and frustrating this knowledge gap is.

sessions.title: Then vs Now: How Learning to Code Changed - And What It Means for All of Us
sessions.speaker: Manar Majdoubi
sessions.abstract: Traditional coding education relied on friction: getting stuck, digging through documentation, and building problem‑solving instincts through trial and error. Today’s learners grow up in an environment shaped by instant answers, AI‑assisted debugging, and interactive guidance.

sessions.title: Conquest, time travel and explosions using Git
sessions.speaker: Alexander Chatzizacharias
sessions.abstract: A talk on git? In this day and age?! Yes. Especially in this day and age. AI agents are running increasingly obscure git commands in our terminals, and most of us just nod along, pretending we know what rerere does. If the machines get to have fun with git, so do we.

sessions.title: When agentic AI makes coding feel like a superpower
sessions.speaker: Alexander Gomez
sessions.abstract: Some time ago I was just typing prompts into a chat window. Last February, I shipped working code from the back of a rollercoaster queue, building with an AI agent on my phone while my kids waited for the ride.

sessions.title: Physically virtual. How information technology obeys physical laws
sessions.speaker: Marianne Hoornenborg
sessions.abstract: What we call virtual is actually physical. Every bit of data we store, move, or erase is represented by a physical state, and every physical system obeys the laws of nature. So let’s look beneath the abstractions of our digital world. What are the physical properties of the systems we handle?

sessions.title: Beyond the Demo: Testing Strategies for Production AI Agents
sessions.speaker: Elena van Engelen
sessions.abstract: AI agents are typically easy to demo but are more difficult to trust on production than traditional software. Not only can they return different results for the same prompt and context, a small prompt change, model switch, or tool response can change the behaviour of the whole application.

sessions.title: DevCulture - The Funny History Nobody Teaches You
sessions.speaker: Jan-Hendrik Kuperus
sessions.abstract: The world wide web turned 35 this year. Java has crossed the magical 30 years. A lot of digital culture stems from the early days when everybody just hacked their wild idea together and put it online because it was fun! Today's web and development work is way too serious.

sessions.title: Snake in 10 Lines: Learning More by Coding Less
sessions.speaker: Guus de Wit
sessions.abstract: Can you create a complete game with just 10 lines of code? That was the quest I set myself when recreating the classic game Snake in as few lines as possible. Let me tell you: I was not ready for the types of challenges I would face.

sessions.title: How playing the trombone makes me a better software engineer - and why you should make music too
sessions.speaker: Marije de Heus
sessions.abstract: Two years ago, I started playing the trombone and immediately fell in love with it. I could never have imagined what an impact it would have on my life and how much it would influence the way I work as a software engineer.

sessions.title: Analytical Java with DuckDB
sessions.speaker: Geertjan Wielenga
sessions.abstract: Your Java service just needs to answer a few analytical questions: top products this month, p95 latency per region, a quick join between a CSV export and a Parquet dump from the data team.

sessions.title: Understanding Prompt Injection - Techniques, Challenges, and Advanced Escalation
sessions.speaker: Brian Vermeer
sessions.abstract: As developers, we’re embracing AI and large language models (LLMs) in our applications more than ever. However, there’s an increasing concern we need to be aware of: prompt injection. This sneaky attack can undermine our AI systems by manipulating the input to produce unintended outputs.

sessions.title: Trick or Treat? The Surprising Link Between Accessibility and Green Software
sessions.speaker: Ramona Domen
sessions.abstract: What if some of the best practices in frontend development came with a double reward? Many of the techniques we use to make applications more accessible, such as faster loading times, simpler interfaces, and efficient use of resources, can also help reduce their environmental impact.

sessions.title: Refactoring Your Brain: Working With ADHD in Engineering Teams
sessions.speaker: Myriam Jessier
sessions.abstract: My brain doesn't have a to-do list, it has eleventeen open tabs and vibes, yet, somehow (most of) the work still gets done. I built an expertise and career off of hyperfocus, lateral thinking, and pattern obsession. This talk does two jobs at once.
